title: McTaggart’s Paradox of Time
scope: Claim-level traceability review of the revised article and matching dataset record. Checked the A-series/B-series distinction; the move from change to the A-series; the incompatibility and successive-predication argument; McTaggart’s tensed reply and regress; the article’s reconstruction caveat; the broad A-/B-theory descriptions; the qualified relativity connection; publication metadata; and ordered source alignment. This is not a judgment that McTaggart’s argument succeeds or that one theory of time is correct.
summary: The revised article now summarizes the A/B distinction and McTaggart’s two-stage argument with the primary text’s relevant pages read in a full-text scan reproduction. It avoids saying the A-properties apply simultaneously, explains the successive-predication reply and regress, and marks the three-premise reconstruction as one standard form because the SEP notes reconstruction disputes. Modern A-/B-theory and relativity statements are qualified to match the SEP discussions. An independent reviewer found no essential correction; the primary scan metadata, article references, and dataset URLs align.

claim_evidence.material_claim: The A-series orders times as future, present, and past, while the B-series orders them through earlier/later relations; McTaggart says genuine change requires the A-series because B-series relations do not change.
claim_evidence.source_title: I.—The Unreality of Time; John M. E. McTaggart
claim_evidence.exact_location: McTaggart pp. 458–465; corroborated by SEP McDaniel §3 and SEP Time §4.
claim_evidence.finding: The primary text supports the distinction and the change argument; the SEP entries corroborate the standard reconstruction. The article attributes the claims to McTaggart rather than presenting them as established facts.
claim_evidence.limitation: The scan is a reproduction and the reconstruction’s details are discussed by later commentators.
claim_evidence.required_edit: Made: clarified the sequence of premises and stated that McTaggart argues B-series relations alone are fixed.

claim_evidence.material_claim: McTaggart argues that incompatible past/present/future determinations apply to each event successively, and that the reply using ‘was future, is present, will be past’ presupposes time and generates a regress.
claim_evidence.source_title: I.—The Unreality of Time; John M. E. McTaggart
claim_evidence.exact_location: McTaggart pp. 468–470; SEP McDaniel §3 on the contradiction argument and its contested reconstruction.
claim_evidence.finding: The primary text supports the successive-predication and regress summary. The revised article does not say that the three properties apply simultaneously and notes that later A-theorists need not treat McTaggart’s objection as decisive.
claim_evidence.limitation: This is a simplified educational summary; it does not establish that the regress is sound or the conclusion follows.
claim_evidence.required_edit: Made: corrected the common simultaneous-predication gloss and explained the tensed reply.

claim_evidence.material_claim: B-theory and A-theory are broad families with multiple positions; presentism and growing block are distinct A-theoretic views, while relativity of simultaneity challenges but does not by itself refute A-theory.
claim_evidence.exact_location: §§5–6, discussion of A-/B-theory, presentism, growing block, and relativity of simultaneity.
claim_evidence.finding: The SEP supports the range-of-views framing and treats relativity as a challenge whose implications depend on additional assumptions. The article explicitly avoids treating physics as a decisive verdict on the metaphysical debate.
claim_evidence.limitation: The article does not survey all A- and B-theories or resolve the metaphysical/physical assumptions.
claim_evidence.required_edit: Made: qualified the relativity connection and separated presentism from growing block.
